validations.resolution: Deprioritized, not resolved. CHIMPs are a mandatory-spending mechanism by definition, and the Crime Victims Fund entry here is mandatory trust-fund plumbing, not a discretionary account. Given the platform is focused on discretionary accounts, a dedicated amount_type or multi-year scorekeeping field is not worth building for this. Left documented for historical accuracy; not blocking Step 3.

FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP) pp. 332, 338, 339, 346: 'In 2026 HRSA will be reorganized into the Agency [p.339: Administration] for a Healthy America to improve coordination of health resources for Americans.' Repeated for 2027 in the FY2027 Appendix (BUDGET-2027-APP) pp. 434, 439, 449. P.L. 119-75 keeps HRSA. Also FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)' -- names HRSA.

Proposed, not enacted. FY2026 Budget Appendix p.360: 'In 2026 SAMHSA will be reorganized into the Agency for a Healthy America to improve coordination of health resources for Americans.' FY2027 Appendix p.464 repeats it for 2027. P.L. 119-75 keeps SAMHSA. Also FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)' -- names SAMHSA.

Not confirmed (owner, 2026-10-06). Proposed type, from explicit text: split_from -- FY2024 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2024-APP, HHS chapter granule BUDGET-2024-APP-1-10, PDF pp. 59 and 64): 'The 2024 Budget requests resources for the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) in a new account, separate from PHSSEF where funding has historically been appropriated.' P.L. 117-328 (FY2023) funds the preparedness programs under the Office of the Secretary's 'Public Health and Social Services Emergency Fund' heading (p.419); P.L. 118-47 (FY2024) has no such heading and an 'Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response' with this heading (p.211).

FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.13 (PDF p.3), Environmental Health: 'National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS): $594.1 million'. Amount match: H.Rept. 119-271 p.342 FY 2026 Request, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health 73,200 (thousands) = $73.2M: the whole NIOSH request. P.L. 119-75 keeps NIOSH under CDC.

FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.14 (PDF p.4), Environmental Health: 'Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act (EEOICPA): $50.8 million in mandatory funding (post-sequester)'. Amount match, pre- vs post-sequester: H.Rept. 119-271 p.342 FY 2026 Request prints 55,358 (thousands), the appropriation before sequestration; 55,358 - 50,800 = 4,558 (8.2%) sequestered. The FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP p.333), AHA's proposed Environmental Health account (075-0386), appropriates the same '$55,358,000' for EEOICPA and shows, in $ millions for 2026: mandatory appropriation 55, permanently reduced -4, mandatory total 51 (= $50.8M rounded). P.L. 119-75 keeps it under CDC.
